An estimation of the $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ decay time for $B^0_s$ mesons has been made with the help of around 37 picobarns of LHCb data from 2010. This measure allows for constraints on theories beyond the Standard Model that may influence the $B^0_s$ system and was found to be 1.440 ± 0.030 (0.023) picoseconds through an fit to $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ decay events, ensuring the removal of wrong-side kaons and compensating for detector effects. The measure can be used to enhance future searches for $B^0_s$ meson oscillations and CP-violating effects.

This research paper focuses on the numerical solution of a stochastic control problem governed by a parabolic equation with the control variable affecting the diffusion coefficient, particularly with the presence of rough inputs; it establishes the convergence of a numerical approximation method and provides a statistical control technique to determine an suitable diffusion-based threshold for the control variable, ensuring that estimated values exceed this limit within a specified subdomain and time frame with high probability; it also includes the development of an efficient numerical discretization and controller, along with an effective density estimation method using kernel estimation.

Our in-depth examination of extremely energetic particles discovered by the Pierre Auger Observatory reveals a significant pattern: the smallest variations in their distribution decline as their energy increases.  A particular energy threshold, beyond which the smallest variations begin examining directional galactic influences, is proposed.  Beyond this threshold, a significant pattern linked to Andromeda galaxy appeared, while the smallest variations remained related to Sagittarius galaxy up to the highest recorded energy.  Extremely limited theoretical investigations into such high-energy particles necessitate focusing on their often neglected directional distribution.  Above 10 EeV, observations demanded more than 10 times their previous error margins, effectively validating prior models and ruling out others.
This paper proves that any finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebra over a given field possesses a specific characteristic - nilpotency, building on a previous discovery that these algebras are solvable.

This study provides first-time data on the fluctuations of a specific angle, known as $\Psi_n$, and magnitude, known as $v_n$, related to particle flow, which have been determined using a newly developed technique for four-particle correlations. Researchers used ALICE to collect these data in high-energy Pb-Pb collisions at the LHC. Fluctuations in both angle and magnitude are evident across different centralities and become more pronounced in more central collisions and in collisions where four particles are being considered. Notably, the $v_n$ fluctuations decrease in Pb-Pb collisions compared to p-Pb and p-Pb' collisions for the same p_T but show a similar pattern as in p-Pb' collisions. Finally, estimates of fluctuations based on hydro simulations match the observed results and constitute an important component of an equation for understanding in-plane and out-of-plane two-particle correlations.

This research focuses on addressing inconsistencies in data tables that contain missing values and functional relationships. Unlike conventional approaches that require adherence to these dependencies, our work aims to explore theories for handling instances that breach certain dependencies, with no preconditions on the presence of missing values. We establish a framework where each data entry can be associated with a truth status: true, false, or undecided. Furthermore, we formulate a set of integrity constraints capable of handling the undecided status. Our investigation yields a comprehensive set of rules to ensure compliance with these constraints, which in turn enable the development of algorithms for verifying tables' consistency. These algorithms' properties are examined and proven, providing a robust method for ensuring data integrity in tables with missing values and functional dependencies.

This study presents a novel dynamic econometric model called Time-Varying Poisson AutoRegressive with external covariates, specifically designed to analyze and forecast count-based time series data. Our research indicates that a score-driven approach is particularly effective in capturing the evolution of time-varying parameters and allows for modeling complex dynamics and shifts within such data sets. Furthermore, we have analyzed the theoretical characteristics of the TV-PARX model, demonstrating under mild conditions that maximum likelihood estimation yields reliable and normally-distributed estimates of model parameters. To evaluate the TV-PARX model's performance and forecasting capabilities in real-world scenarios, we conducted a series of Monte Carlo simulations. Additionally, we have applied the time-varying specification of the TV-PARX model to empirical data sets, analyzing new daily COVID-19 cases in Italy and corporate defaults in the US.

We introduce Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs), a novel object representation that
replicates both object points and relative poses in relation to a target, using
category-level descriptors. We apply this representation in object manipulation,
with the aim of repeating tasks on new object instances from the same category
after witnessing a single demonstration. To achieve this, we use optimization
to locate the pose whose descriptor corresponds to that in the demonstration. NDFs
are efficiently trained without expert input, using a self-supervised 3D
auto-encoder, and exhibit robust performance across 6-DoF rotations and translations.
In experiments, NDFs master tasks from just a handful (5-10) demonstrations,
in both simulation and with a physical robot. Results show our method excels at
generalizing over different object instances and poses, surpassing a comparison
method relying on 2D descriptors. The NDF project is hosted at https://yilundu.github.io/ndf/.

Using the functional renormalization group at the next-to-leading order in the derivative expansion, we have updated the position of the Yang-Lee edge singularity for O(N) universality classes in classic scenarios. Specifically for QCD's relevant universality classes in three dimensions, we have determined $|z_c|/R_\chi^{1/\gamma}$ to be approximately 1.607, 1.589 for $N=2, 4$ respectively. Alternatively, we have previously found $|z_c|$ to be around 2.03, 1.68 for $N=2, 4$ although these earlier results have a larger systematic uncertainty.

In statistics and machine learning, it is frequently essential to establish whether a basic optimization method on a non-convex function can eventually enter a region where the function becomes locally convex. To address this, we developed an inequality that enables us to analyze the properties of the optimization landscape surrounding the solutions found by an approximate message passing (AMP) algorithm. Specifically, we applied our inequality to demonstrate the local convexity of a particular TAP free energy function, which is relevant to the Z2 synchronization problem and the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model. Additionally, our inequality led to a confirmation of a previous conjecture made in relation to a problem involving the estimation of a sparse signal from noisy observations.

While using photometry from stars to monitor the atmosphere may seem uncomplicated for optical astrophysics, achieving a precision of 0.1% in measuring the size and impact of aerosol particles remains challenging. By reanalyzing the results from such measurements, we determined the sizes of the aerosol particles by linking them to well-known meteorological and meteoro-optical phenomena and are examining further links with surface pollution sources and atmospheric gas concentrations. To improve the accuracy of these measurements, we suggest revising the photometric filtering systems they rely on. By using aerosol data derived from astronomical sources to complement traditional measurement methods, we anticipate gaining deeper insights into the Earth's aerosol composition.

Recently, estimating a 6D object pose using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) has gained significant interest. Literature can be broadly divided into two main streams based on whether intermediate cues are employed: direct methods that regress object poses directly and two-stage pipelines where CNN extracts features before a traditional method estimates poses. Combining the efficiency of direct methods with the robustness of two-stage pipelines, this paper presents a novel framework for 6D pose estimation called DeepHMap++, which incorporates a correspondence learning module to supplement the pose regression module. Specifically, the correspondence learning module comprises a projection grouping network and a correspondence loss, which in comparison to using raw intermediate features, employ processed features that have higher discriminative power. Experiments conducted on the OHN dataset demonstrate the performance of this model, achieving mean average errors of 2.04 and 5.01 for rotational and translational poses, respectively, which outperforms the state-of-the-art two-stage methods.

We present GGLasso, a Python library designed to address General Graphical Lasso
challenges. Based on the original work of Friedman (2007), Graphical Lasso
estimates a sparsely constructed inverse covariance matrix $\Theta$ from
multivariate Gaussian data $\mathcal{X}$, initially introduced by Dempster (1972)
under Covariance Selection. The framework has been expanded to accommodate
elliptically symmetric, t-distributed, and non-negative datasets. We demonstrate
that each variant can be methodically addressed using the same fundamental
algorithm. To handle large-scale datasets and vary the variable threshold $\gamma$
efficiently, GGLasso employs memory-optimal storage strategies and a concise matrix
representation known as the COO format. The package features robust solutions,
visualization tools for results and theoretical comparisons, and a suite of
tests utilizing synthetic and real-world data sets.

Numerous numerical methods for resolving stochastic differential equations in molecular dynamics simulations have been scrutinized and assessed, focusing on deterministic impulses, drifts, and Brownian motions. By utilizing the Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff expansion, recent studies found that the methods' accuracy could be evaluated in terms of the impact of the step size on configurational averaging. Results showed that for harmonic oscillators, some methods yield precise configurational averages, potentially leading to better performance in biomolecular simulations, especially in cases where bond stretching modes exhibit anharmonic behavior. Furthermore, research found that biologically relevant simulations could benefit significantly from using methods that offer precise configurational averaging, as they require fewer simulations to achieve a target level of precision when comparing atomistic models with coarse-grained models.

Our new method calculates a variation of eigenvector centrality for multi-layered networks that incorporate node importance across different layers. In these networks, defined by separate interconnected graphs without connections between different layers, the value of a node's centrality is determined by the sum of the values of the connected nodes within each specific layer, similar to traditional eigenvector centrality calculations. Unlike standard approaches, our approach takes into account the relationships between different network layers and their respective impact on the centrality values. Unlike current multi-layer eigenvector centrality frameworks that account for inter-layer connections, our approach uses a separate set of equations that can be solved using a hybrid algorithm.

Recently, we generated the $R$-Poincar\'e algebra using deformed Poisson brackets, 
which effectively replicate the Fock coordinate transformation. This transformation 
corresponds to a de Sitter spacetime. In this study, we formulate the Dirac equation within 
$R$-Minkowski spacetime and establish that it is analogous to the Dirac equation defined 
within the de Sitter spacetime, described by its conformally flat metric. We then propose 
a novel strategy to solve the Dirac equation within the de Sitter spacetime by adopting 
the Schr\"{o}dinger picture.

This study investigates how spheres interact with water upon impact, specifically the process known as surface seal that occurs as the sphere enters the water's surface. This surface seal regime, found between low and high-speed impact velocities, features a distinctive "splash dome" formation. Empirical rules describing when the splash dome closes, based on the impact velocity and water's viscosity, are presented for the first time. These rules show that the relevant depth of water affected by the sphere is minimal and largely unaffected by viscosity, whereas the depth at which closure occurs varies significantly with viscosity. The limitations of these rules are demonstrated, particularly in cases where the splash dome closes too deeply or with little depth beneath the sphere. The applicable range of the surface seal regime and its transition to other impact velocities are further explored.

A well-known hypothesis posits that gravity at a quantum level must be devoid of universal symmetries. We studied an array of Type IIB four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ effective field theories to uncover the range of universal symmetries potentially present and then investigated why they are avoided. Generalized $\theta$-terms emerge as crucial elements in these theories. These $\theta$-terms generate nonlinear connections between axion fields and quadratic gauge field strengths which can be used to break many universal symmetries. If we consider charged states as part of the scenario, additional universal symmetries may be destroyed, yet we found that the $\theta$-terms yield a Witten-like effect that indicates that the range of charged states is composed of an endlessly populated, lattice-like spectrum generated by BPS states with an exceptionally low mass.

Our calculations using first-principles methods reveal that cubanite exhibits unusual orbital selectivity, with electrons occupying certain molecular orbitals while being absent in other equivalent orbitals. This phenomenon is particularly prominent in the metal sub-lattice and is caused by strong spin-orbit coupling, which creates an energy gap between the filled molecular orbitals and the partially filled $t_{2g}$ and $e_{g}$ d-orbitals. This explanation is backed by calculations that show increased orbital selectivity when spin-orbit coupling is included, as well as comparisons with related minerals such as violarite and heazlewoodite. Violarite exhibits only mild orbital polarization, whereas heazlewoodshows only mild orbital polarization, whereas heazlewoodite displays very strong orbital polarization.

A burgeoning field in quantum physics, known as multi-phonon physics, is driving research and development for both fundamental understanding and applications in metrology and communication systems. Quantum acoustic resonators serve as the ideal testing ground for multi-phonon phenomena through a combination of theoretical and experimental studies. The specific system studied consists of a semiconductor quantum dot driven by a laser, coupled to an acoustic cavity, and has exhibited remarkable multi-phonon properties, albeit previously described with a simplistic two-level quantum dot model. However, by accounting for both bright and dark excitons within the model, the complexity of the system becomes apparent. Notably, researchers have observed a particularly large Rabi oscillation with the application of a massive 1.17 GHz coupling to a single phonon mode, occurring in the absence of an external magnetic field.

Our investigation focuses on a 2D electronic lattice from a non-symmorphic wallpaper group, specifically focusing on a centered rectangular lattice type. We've discovered that a 3-band Hamiltonian, when paired with spin freedom, forms a controllable trefoil knot within this lattice. The position and orientation of these knot components can be adjusted by modifying the system's parameters. The analysis reveals that by tuning these parameters, we can facilitate the coexistence of multiple pairs of linearly interacting bands by eliminating the mass terms in the effective Dirac Hamiltonian. Notably, the lattice's non-symmorphic characteristics allow us to locate multiple knot components near the high-symmetry boundaries without the need to violate certain constraints. Furthermore, we developed an analytical approach to map the conditions under which massless regions emerge. Ultimately, we demonstrated that varying the system's parameters can lead to the simultaneous occurrence of various T-shaped massless regions.

Quantum states known as single-photon catalyzed coherent states (SPCCSs) can be generated via quantum-optical catalysis using beam splitters or parametric amplifiers. These states occur when a coherent state and a single-photon state interact in two input ports, and a photon is detected in a specific output channel. We examine the success probabilities associated with detecting these states, as they vary depending on the catalytic device used. Notably, our analysis reveals that states produced by beam splitters and parametric amplifiers exhibit the same characteristics when analyzing the distribution of photons. We thoroughly investigate the unique quantum properties of SPCCSs, including sub-Poisson statistics, anti-bunching effects, and quadrature squeezing. These findings demonstrate that SPCCSs possess abundant non-classical behavior, thereby conferring a quantum advantage for executing various technological tasks.

In General Relativity using the Newman-Penrose formalism, the use of bivectors plays a key role in identifying the precise solutions to Einstein's field equations. This review focuses on explaining the fundamental principles and detailed calculations of bivectors within the Newman-Penrose formalism, specifically by converting a complex self-dual electromagnetic field from the standard Minkowski space basis to the complex null tetrad basis. As a result, we derive the complex coefficients of the Weyl tensor in the context of Newman-Penrose formalism.

A recent framework combining artificial neural networks and mixed integer linear programming for designing chemical compounds has been built upon to create a new method for polymer inference. This new method incorporates a unique way of depicting polymers using monomers, new descriptors that capture their structure, and employs linear regression in the predictive framework. Computational trials have demonstrated that the proposed approach excels in predicting specific chemical properties in polymers, also successfully modeling compounds composed of up to 50 non-hydrogen atoms within a monomeric structure.

Identifying tumors in the esophagus from CT scans can be very difficult for humans or computer systems due to low contrast, the varying shape of the esophagus, and the presence of external objects such as feeding tubes. To compensate for these difficulties, doctors often rely on supplementary information from other imaging techniques, medical histories, and endoscopic findings. Acquiring and combining these sources of information is time-consuming and sometimes impossible, particularly in emergency cases. In this study, we investigate the potential of a deep learning technique to automatically identify tumors in the esophagus from CT scans alone. To achieve this, we developed a deep learning architecture called DDAUnet, which is based on a attention-unet model and enhanced with dense connections. DDAUnet successfully identified tumors in the esophagus with high precision, recall, and a dice similarity t-score of 0.85 on the MedU-SEG dataset. These results indicate that a single deep learning technique can produce accurate results, comparable to those obtained when using multi-modality data.

Multilingual individuals possess a high level of proficiency in two or more languages, enabling effective written and oral communication across multiple languages. When communicating, they may blend languages, also known as code-switching or code-mixing, by switching between different languages within a single utterance. This research explores current NLP developments, constraints, and potential obstacles in tackling five critical issues affecting multilingual communities: crisis management, healthcare, election campaigns, fake news dissemination, and hate speech. To move forward, we outline potential future datasets, models, and resources to enhance NLP applications for societal betterment, exemplified through an analysis of code-mixing between English and Hindi but with implications for other language combinations.

Human-generated descriptions are commonly used to train and evaluate image description systems, which are ranked based on their similarity to these descriptions. This method's reliability is supported by comparisons with annotated captions on images. However, research demonstrates that when carefully crafted descriptions are employed to both train and assess these systems, their performance will deteriorate. This effect is even more severe when deep learning techniques are utilized. Our findings are particularly relevant to the assessment of systems like those presented in He (2019) and Parmar et al. (2018).

Tantalum oxide compounds, with the formula Ta$_2$O$_5$, are distinguished by unique properties including high dielectric values and minimal reflectivity. Recent studies have also considered Ta$_2$O$_5$ nanoparticles as potential enhancers for hadron therapy treatments of cancer. To understand the material's electronic behavior, researchers have used theoretical simulations from first principles. Yet, Ta$_2$O$_5$ has various forms, complicating attempts to identify their individual properties. To resolve this issue, researchers used simulations to determine the most accurate initial structure for Ta$_2$O$_5$'s non-periodic state, using a combination of methods to calculate its electronic structure, including its magnetic properties and charge transfers between tantalum atoms. The study found that the proposed ground state structure aligns with experimental Ta$_2$O$_5$ data, providing confirmation for the predicted non-periodic state in certain Ta-oxide compounds.

Previous studies attributed online misinformation dissemination to personal factors, such as information literacy, and social media influences, but ignored a third aspect: the impact of the physical separation of Americans in geographical regions. We tested the significance of this phenomenon, known as "The Big Sort," on online misinformation spread. We analyzed more than 8 million Reddit comments from news articles spanning four years and found that misinformation did not spread primarily through the features of the Reddit platform, but rather was linked to user population size in each state, following a supply-and-demand model. Furthermore, variations in misinformation dissemination were explained by local personality traits and cultural characteristics rather than economic, social, or political conditions. In areas where residents are less diligent in nature, and cultures place little emphasis on adherence to norms, we found increased circulation of all news, including credible sources.

Humans employ spoken language to efficiently teach other people various skills. Although robotic demonstrations are a natural teaching method, learning from solely observed actions does not take full advantage of audio feedback from instructors. To effectively incorporate auditory cues, it's essential to understand their meaning. This study aims to analyze and interpret the verbal content heard during robotic instruction by having annotators actively listen to and process human-instructed audio along with the accompanying task being demonstrated to a robot. The Annotated Instruction Dataset (AAD) comprises 50 carefully crafted annotations derived from a single audio source. The study seeks to utilize such annotated data to apply sophisticated natural language processing techniques, ultimately facilitating robotic conversation analysis.

Quantum field theory complexity is particularly hard to define, especially when transitioning beyond simple free models and their corresponding Gaussian representations. A promising approach to address this difficulty is through the study of conformal field theories in 1+1 dimensions, specifically focusing on the universal sector of the energy-momentum tensor in this context. A key unifying framework consists of Euler-Arnold equations along with their associated conserved currents, leading to a set of exact equations that describe the time evolution of complexity. A rigorous derivation of these equations is from the Ward-Takahashi identities in conformal gravity, and solutions are found in terms of initial conditions and their conserved currents, leading to a rigorous differential equation for the rate of change of complexity.

Conversational interfaces are becoming ubiquitous, and systems with these interfaces are being widely used in various settings by many individuals. Although they have achieved considerable success, the infrastructure for automated testing of these systems lags behind traditional software systems. To enhance the quality of conversational systems, developers require a robust automated testing framework that streamlines the process of crafting, executing, and updating test cases. This paper outlines our ongoing research in developing an automated testing framework for conversational agents in Python, and highlights the key challenges faced in this endeavor. Specifically, we highlight the difficulties in establishing a precise specification for desired system behavior and comparing the meaning of utterances.

Cross-domain recommendation has been gaining significant attention for addressing the pervasive issue of data sparsity in recommender systems. Single-target and dual-target CDR approaches are often hindered by the limitations of requiring at least one well-supplied domain and over-reliance on domain-agnostic preferences, which is impractical given the ubiquitous sparsity in real-world scenarios. To address these shortcomings, we introduce a novel framework called Multi-Sparse-Domain Collaborative Recommendation (MSDCR) that tackles multi-target cross-domain recommendation in multiple sparse domains. In contrast to conventional CDR methods, MSDCR considers all participating domains as equally data-poor, thereby simultaneously enhancing the recommendation performance across each domain. We devise a Multi-Domain Separation Network (MDSN) and a Gated Aspect Preference Enhancement (GAPE) module to augment a user's specific aspect preferences in each domain by transferring complementary preferences from other domains, while maintaining domain-specific uniqueness through adversarial training and dynamically determining the degree of complementarity using the GAPE module. Furthermore, we introduce a Multi-Domain Adaptation Network (MDAN) to capture a user's general, domain-agnostic aspect preference. By integrating the domain-specific aspect preference and the domain-agnostic aspect preference, we aim to achieve a thorough understanding of a user's aspect preference in each domain. Convex optimization issues often take on a more manageable form when represented with conic formulations that leverage a wide variety of exotic cones. Exotic cones in this context, refer to specialized geometric shapes with properties enabling efficient implementation in solving optimization problems. This discussion will focus on a framework for handling these shapes naturally by utilizing a leading open-source tool, Hypatia.jl, which provides access to a diverse array of these shapes. The framework and tooling enable the development of intricate and user-friendly formulations that can be efficiently solved with solvers compatible with the shapes in use. The proposed method will be demonstrated and tested through a collection of practical applications and challenging mathematical problems whose solutions involve dominant cones this framework is built around.

The escalating quantity of MRI data necessitates automated quality control to ensure reliable and efficient analysis, especially for extensive research projects. Several approaches have been explored to develop scalable and dependable quality control pipelines, but effectively generalizing these methods across diverse, previously unseen data remains a significant challenge. This study evaluated the MRIQC pipeline's performance on multiple large datasets, utilizing ABIDE and OASIS as examples, and compared its results with manual ratings given by human experts. Human annotators provided quality scores for both research images included in these datasets and randomly selected images for OASIS. For quality classification, we evaluated supervised learning models, contrasting the outcomes when using only MRI data QC features versus a combination of QC and metadata features. Our findings show that existing tools can produce quality control datasets with actionable data quality scores and evaluation models derived from these datasets achieved high precision-recall areas (0.70 for OASIS, 0.65 for OASIS+OASIS-QC, and 0.50 for OASIS-QC), although generalizing to new datasets remains a non-negligible challenge that calls for further investigation.

To understand how private electric vehicles influence the recovery of power grids following outages, we developed a mathematical framework that incorporates decentralized decision-making in both transportation and energy systems. We utilized multi-agent optimization to model this process and overcame computational challenges through an efficient algorithm based on precise reformation. Numerical analysis was conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, yielding valuable policy insights and paving the way for further study into grid resilience with private EVs within interconnected transportation and energy networks.

The Motivation Dynamics framework, a concept explored in recent studies that applies bifurcations to model an autonomous vehicle's decision-making processes, is further developed to accommodate multiple autonomous vehicles. We apply this framework to a multi-agent scenario where vehicles must meet at a specific location. Our analysis of this model reveals that it can capture the autonomous vehicles' recurrent meeting behavior. A computational experiment validates the theoretical findings and confirms the suitability of this framework to model real-world multi-agent meetups.

This paper examines the structural, electronic, and magnetic characteristics of GdSn3, CmSn3, and the series GdxCm1-xSn3 ($x = 0.25$, $0.5$, and $0.75$) using a full-potential linearized augmented plane wave method within the generalized gradient approximation+U. We studied the fundamental properties of bulk GdSn3, CmSn3, and GdxCm1-xSn3 materials crystallizing in the AuCu3 structure type (space group: Fm-3m). According to our findings, all of these materials exhibit a direct band gap in the gamma point and show characteristics of half-metallical behavior with Gd and Cm displaying localized magnetic moments. Notably, the CmSn3 band gap is about twice the size of GdSn3. The magnetic moments of Gd and Cm in all calculated samples show inverse relationship to their respective atomic moments, and the total magnetic moments of these materials result from the combination of Sn and the rare earth elements' contributions. Additionally, the total magnetic moments of all calculated samples with interstitial Hf and Si atom substitutions demonstrate direct proportionality to the 5d rare earth 5d elements' magnetic moments. A possible new kind of baryon is predicted based on the top quark's unique properties. Given that top quarks decay too quickly to form usual baryons, we've identified a potential new baryonic state composed of a top quark and a pair of antistrange strange particles. Due to the strong attraction between this particle and its antistrange strange counterpart, it may become trapped as an $\bar{s}s\top$-onium. Calculated results for this $\bar{s}s\Top$ hadron show that it could be slightly more massive than the corresponding $\bar{s}s t$-onium state, although the latter's existence is unlikely given the repulsion between the two top quarks. If this $\bar{s}s\Top$ state does exist, it might be detectable at particle colliders like the LHC or future FCC, particularly because it would be highly unstable and decay into strange quark pairs. Additionally, calculations suggest that colliders could also produce exotic hybrid or tetraquark states made of top quarks and anti-strange particles, potentially including an $s s \top \bar{s}$-onium with a mass around 350 GeV.

The concept of ordered generating sequences (OGS) extends a fundamental property of finite abelian groups to non-abelian groups, providing a distinct generalization. According to its definition, any element within a group can be expressed as a product of various generator powers, arranged in a specific order. For the symmetric group Sn, R. Shwartz established a significant link between the ordered generating sequences and the standard Coxeter presentation. Our study extends this connection to the finite classical Coxeter group Bn by standardizing the ordered generating sequences, which allows us to identify exchange laws for Bn. Moreover, we establish a connection between the standard ordered generating sequences, Coxeter length, and the descent set of Bn.

Utilizing the Pantheon SN Ia dataset and Sloan Digital Sky Survey, we've developed a method to calculate weak lensing convergence by combining data on the positions and photometry of foreground galaxies. A correlation between this approach and the residual Hubble diagram values of Type Ia supernovae holds a $3.6\sigma$ significance and is consistent with dark matter effects due to galactic halos. Furthermore, we constrained galactic halo properties, including the mass-to-light ratio $\Gamma$ and the radial distribution of matter density within haloes $\rho(r)$. Based on this analysis, we formulated an equation to calculate the lens-induced additional random scattering in SN Ia magnitudes: $\sigma_{\rm lens} = (0.08 \pm 0.04) \cdot (d_{\rm C}(z)/ d_{\rm C}(1))^{3/2}$. As a result, the lens-induced apparent magnitude dispersion will approach the same magnitude as intrinsic SN Ia scatter at $z \approx 1.2$. By incorporating the effects of weak lensing, we can potentially detect a break in the Pantheon SN Ia power spectrum beyond this z value.

The development of efficient and controllable quantum communication networks will depend heavily on reliable creation and manipulation of solid-state devices that interface photons with electronic spins effectively. In silicon material, T-type damage centers have shown significant potential for this interface, thanks to their unique optical properties in the O-band region and long-lived electronic and nuclear spin lifetimes. Although research on these defect centers has so far been conducted as part of bulk silicon studies, we demonstrate the consistent creation of high T center densities within the 220nm device layer of Silicon-On-Insulator (SOI) wafers, using a process that combines ion implantation and heat treatment. By developing a method to measure spin-dependent optical transitions, we found that high T center densities located near the interface can exhibit ~1 GHz levels of spectral diffusion without the need for extensive optimization of the fabrication process.

For our task that considers context, a suitable object detector is needed.
Different object detectors exploit scene context for recognition in varying ways.
This study categorizes object detectors into 3 groups based on context usage:
one that doesn't use context by isolating the input, another that uses partial
context by isolating part of the feature map, and one that uses full context
without isolation.
Our evaluation method assesses the effect of context for each deep detector
category systematically. A specially designed dataset is created to test the
effect of context for deep detectors. The impact of removing the background
context and foreground objects on the MS COCO is also examined.
It is shown that both two-stage and single-stage object detectors can make use
of the context due to their extensive receptive field.
Thus, selecting the best object detector for a particular application depends
on the specific context in question.

The main objective of this paper is to investigate multiple solution possibilities for a specific Kirchhoff type elliptic system of equations that are given by the system of equations where $m\left(\sum^k_{j=1}\|u_j\|^2\right)\Delta u_i=\frac{f_i(x,u_1,\ldots,u_k)}{|x|^\beta}+\varepsilon h_i(x)$ holds for $i=1,\ldots,k$, within the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^N$.

We examine the concentration behavior of functionals of random vectors whose entries reside in the discrete cube. These vectors must adhere to either the stochastic covering property or the strong Rayleigh property. Our findings provide discrete counterparts to continuous inequalities, maintaining the same exponential factors in their bounds for both DC-spaces and log-concave measures on the discrete cube, as initially established in recent studies. Specifically, we demonstrate that for any function $f$ within a set of functions with bounded influence, the probability of the measure of functions with a $f$-norm less than or equal to 1 exceeding a certain exponential threshold, is greater than a given value, is at most 64 times the probability of the set of functions with a 1-norm of the square root of the maximum influence less than or equal to 1. Furthermore, a comparable inequality for the $1$-norm is also derived. These results have additional implications, including the derivation of inequalities for functions of binary variables under the AND-OR graph dependency notion and those that are monotone with respect to the T0-topology.

Wilberd van der Kallen translated this 1951 thesis into English, originally written by T.A. Springer. Springer investigated the method of categorizing conjugacy classes within the symplectic group Sp_n(K), specifically focusing on fields K with a characteristic other than two. His work revealed that each conjugacy class can be distinguished using a combination of invariant characteristics. These characteristics initially mirror those found in the general linear group – namely, irreducible polynomials and systems of non-negative integers – but also incorporate additional properties, such as unique configurations of Hermitian forms and quadratic forms, each belonging to a specific equivalence class.

A key obstacle in kidney transplants arises from the incompatibility between donors and patients, which has been exacerbated by the growing scarcity of kidney donors. Desensitization techniques were developed to overcome the immunological difficulties. Patients receiving incompatible transplants face a higher risk of transplant rejection, infections, and cancer, and are more likely to lose their transplants. We aim to find the optimal acceptance criteria for end-stage kidney patients by potentially receiving incompatible kidneys. A Markov Decision Process model is introduced, which accounts for the level of incompatibility as a key factor, making it a more complex problem to solve, but with suitable conditions, it is possible to establish control limit policies that can be easily applied. Our study uses numerical examples to demonstrate how the optimal policy behaves under different levels of incompatibility, and highlights the significance of taking incompatibility into consideration in decision-making, especially when desensitization treatments are available.

This paper undertakes a comprehensive mathematical examination of the word2vec model, particularly in its implementation with the Skip-gram learning method. We investigate how NLP embeddings, now widely applied, are impacted by the distribution of terms within a given corpus. A mathematical framework is employed to elucidate the implicit structural assumptions of the model, revealing how it can effectively capture relationships between terms that possess frequent associations with one another, regardless of explicit grammatical connections. We demonstrate empirically using NLP and symbolic computation tools, including Mathematica, that the model learns the fundamental principles of grammatical syntax, allowing it to infer complex linguistic connections, such as those between related terms with opposing emotional connotations. We further explore a critical application of this model in corporate financial reporting, specifically in terms of its capacity to classify positive and negative emotional content. Our research highlights an enigmatic challenge where the model mistakens emotionally neutral content for a positive category, a crucial discovery with implications for the accurate analysis of emotional content in written communication.

This article presents the SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM based IDET systems as alternatives to our previously proposed optimal wideband waveforming strategy in [1].
Fair-throughput and sum-throughput optimisation problems are defined and formulated.
By leveraging an algorithm that utilizes fixed points, we derive the optimal fair-throughput and sum-throughput values for SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM systems.

This research introduces a new method to model the interaction of fluids with changing phases, combining level-set and embedded boundary techniques. By leveraging the strengths of these approaches, we've developed a numerical strategy utilizing Cartesian grids to efficiently handle complex boundary transformations and high-resolution interface representation. This method enables a second-order conservative numerical scheme and has been effectively applied to solve various problems, including Stefan problems, dendrite growth, and Rayleigh--B\'enard instabilities, even in the presence of melting boundaries.

In multiagent learning settings beyond finding equilibria, learning rationalizable behavior is another important goal. However, existing algorithms focus primarily on rationalizability in zero-sum games, not the broader range of outcomes that can be rational. This work develops and analyzes rationalizable multiagent learning algorithms for general-sum games, beginning with an ER learning framework that guarantees outcomes within the set of outcomes that can be rational, and then presenting a novel asynchronous R-learning algorithm with strong convergence properties. Both methods demonstrate strong rationalizability and average regret bounds, and our results are supported by empirical data.

An analysis of a stochastic Susceptible to Infective to Recovered model is conducted, where the model is based on an Erdős-Rényi random graph that changes dynamically as susceptible individuals connected to infected neighbours form new connections or sever existing ones. As the model is scaled to accommodate large populations, researchers obtained mathematical proofs of key properties of the model, particularly its early stages and the phase where the epidemic spreads rapidly. They also found that under certain conditions, there are sharp thresholds where the model suddenly switches between two completely different behaviours. It has been proven that these transitions are more dramatic if the model is changed to only form new connections to uninfected individuals, where the model suddenly switches from no infections to complete spread.

Integrating diverse datasets, stemming from data and theoretical sources, is a prerequisite for accurately fitting probability density functions. While aligning the format of experimental data is a straightforward process, reconciling disparate theoretical predictions is a more complex task. Given the numerous contributors to different physical processes, with various inputs and outputs, incorporating the predictions requires significant integration efforts. Furthermore, since processes are often measured across a wide range of scales, evolution equations such as DGLAP need to be applied to PDF candidates or already incorporated into the predictions. Given the computational intensity of these calculations, it is beneficial to automate the process by linking the scale of calculations to the desired accuracy, and by connecting the format of predictions to the underlying physics. In this context, a computational framework has been developed to fit PDFs, which imports predictions for various processes with different numbers of included orders, thereby allowing for a high-accuracy fit to be achieved. This framework, known as rootpdf, is built upon root and includes a collection of tools for processing predictions, with the format of each input file precisely defined. The computational framework can be customized to fit the specific requirements of a given fit, by simply plugging in the desired processes in a particular sequence. It has been demonstrated that this pipeline can be used to perform a global fit for both CT18 and HERAPDF1.2 PDF sets.

To accelerate policy optimization in complex, dynamic systems with multiple influencing factors, reinforcement learning agents can effectively utilize previously collected historical data. Standard experience replay enables agents to retain information from prior iterations. However, the current approach equally values all collected observations, neglecting their varying significance. A more adaptive method, the variance reduction based experience replay framework, selectively leverages the most informative historical data. This approach prioritizes past observations more likely to represent the current target distribution. Theoretical and practical evaluations demonstrate that this method accelerates optimal policy discovery and boosts the effectiveness of state-of-the-art policy optimization methods.

In our analysis of conversational dialogue, we face numerous possible responses 
to any given history, leading us to present the MultiTalk Dataset. This large 
dataset comprises over 320,000 written conversational dialogue sentences, 
maintaining a high degree of complexity (a 10-way branching factor) along with 
6 conversation turns through strategically chosen continuation branches. Our study 
of dialogue generation involves multiple advancements, particularly in highly 
branching scenarios. To evaluate the diversity of generated text, we introduce a 
simple scoring algorithm grounded in bipartite graph matching, effectively 
incorporating various references. Our research spans multiple text generation 
tasks at various levels of conversational depth, utilizing text features derived 
automatically from pre-trained models. Ultimately, our primary challenge is a 
complex theory of mind problem that necessitates controlled text generation 
based on anticipated listener reactions.

We developed a technique for creating rapid, comprehensive N-body simulation datasets for a broad range of modified gravity models by utilizing two existing gravitational solvers, $R_{2}$ and $C_{0}$, both of which are deeply connected to general relativity. Our approach enables the generation of simulated datasets with $N$ particle simulations in a significantly shorter time frame compared to existing $N$-body methods, offering $2$ to $3$ orders of magnitude efficiency gains at different radius ranges. In a practical demonstration, we generated $100$ to $1000$ particle simulated datasets for an $888$ $h^{-1}$Mpc cosmological volume in as little as a few to a couple of dozen seconds, including a calculation of the function describing radial acceleration deviations from $2$ to $3$ to $9$ to 10 powers. Both existing solvers exhibit a distinct characteristic where they behave in a uniquely mapped radius range but exhibit a highly suppressive, power-law response in the opposite range, allowing for the efficient combination of their simulated datasets with minimal loss of precision. We also provide a comprehensive set of guidance for utilizing our technique for the purpose of carrying out precise cosmological simulated data analyses in a vast range of modified gravity models.

Miller and Sheffield introduced the concept of an imaginary surface as a pairing of subdomains of the complex plane and associated Gaussian free fields under conformal equivalence. Specifically, they considered the relationship between these pairings and chordal Schramm-Loewner evolution. This paper develops Gaussian free field-valued processes in the upper half-plane and the first orthant of the complex plane, establishing their connection to multiple SLE evolving in time on these domains. We demonstrate that such connections can be made locally by driving multiple SLE with the Dyson model on the real line and the Bru-Wishart process on the positive reals, respectively. Ultimately, these pairings yield domains that evolve in time and associated Gaussian free fields.

MediaWiki's 'WorkingWiki' is an open-source extension that converts a wiki
into a sophisticated collaborative platform for developing high-quality manuscripts
and software projects. Originally developed at McMaster University's theoretical
biology lab, WorkingWiki enables multiple users to work together on a range of
tasks by utilizing command-line tools to translate raw'source code' into desired outputs.
Its features cater specifically to programmers and researchers who use languages
like R, Python, and C, and it boasts specialized tools for managing references
using BibTeX and LaTeX. To demonstrate its versatility, we have created and
made available the R-for-reproducing-nature-cranach-data-package on our server,
and we have designed the application so that others can easily adapt it for
their own uses on platforms like GitHub and GitLab.

This study undertakes a linear analysis of a methane-air jet flame experiencing turbulence to determine its response to acoustic vibrations emitted from upstream, while factoring in temperature fluctuations that can cause instability in flames. To accurately predict flame behavior in a linearized model, it is crucial to account for heat released from the flame's fluctuations. Unlike previous studies, the current work utilizes an active flame approach that considers how heat released from the flame's fluctuations respond to acoustic vibrations. To apply this approach, the combustion process is modelled using Fourier-Bessel expansions, while flow field variables are represented through experimental data obtained from existing works. Results show that response patterns vary significantly among different flames due to their distinct release profiles, and that transport of thermal energy expansions across different lengths can lead to axial modes of resonance within the pipe. Furthermore, the research reveals that flame geometry impacts the absorption of energy emitted from the pipe's open end, and that installation of a flame with a curved tip guide can reduce stress on the flame by filtering out dangerous frequencies.

We investigate the neutrinoless double beta decay driven by an extremely light dark matter field interacting with neutrinos, particularly focusing on an axion-like particle. Two novel parameters that influence the neutrinoless double beta decay magnitude are introduced and incorporated into a global analysis, which also considers cosmological observations. Notably, if the dark matter is composed of these ultra-light particles, an enlarged neutrino mass matrix derived from the cosmological data constricores the conventional neutrinoless double beta decay parameter, despite not yet observing this process experimentally. Furthermore, time-dependent neutrinoless double beta decay is an inherent prediction of this model, which can be tested in upcoming experiments. However, the oscillating behavior of the dark matter field hinders the ability to determine the neutrinoless double beta decay rate. We discuss the necessary conditions and potential modifications to carry out this measurement. Furthermore, an analysis of the parameters that could allow for a detectable signal and an assessment of the feasibility of this approach are conducted.

Nonlocal gravity theory is a classical generalization of Einstein's gravity theory. Based on an analogy with nonlocal electrodynamics, this new model involves a history-dependent relation that can be confirmed through data. The purpose of this paper is to modify nonlocal gravity theory so that the nonlocal aspect relates directly to observable properties, similar to the approach in nonlocal electrodynamics. The reformulated theory results in a constitutive relation identical to one proposed recently by Puetzfeld, Obukhov, and Hehl. The nonlocal gravity theory can be applied to show that de Sitter spacetime does not meet the theory's requirements.

We developed a new approach to identify causal genetic variations and study the causes of certain traits by combining results from genome-wide association analyses with a type of genetic information known as summary statistics from various genomic studies.  This technique led to significant findings in 14 out of 18 human traits we tested, revealing areas of the genome that are responsible for specific traits and associated genes that contribute to them.  For instance, our study found variances in chromatin structure in different parts of the genome that are linked to traits such as Crohn's disease, breast cancer, and type 2 diabetes, and identified genes and proteins that are related to biological processes that cause these traits.  Additionally, our approach could distinguish signals from known associations and found regions of the genome that are responsible for certain traits even when current association studies failed to find them.  By incorporating a wide range of genomic information, our method outperformed when used individually but struggled to isolate causal variations and study the causes of certain traits and diseases despite its success in achieving broader associations.

This paper discusses recent findings from the LHC involving small systems studied
by the ALICE, ATLAS and CMS collaborations. Due to the growing significance
of QCD in small systems, particularly in situations with high multiplicity, not all
observations made in heavy-ion collisions can be directly applied to interpret the
data from small systems. Furthermore, the concept of "vol. per nucleon pair"
is problematic in certain situations. Nevertheless, the heavy-ion results provide
valuable frameworks that may be useful in interpreting the quark-gluon plasma
formed in small systems. Some small-system collisions may even produce multiple
nuclei interactions simultaneously, potentially leading to a small amount of quark-gluon plasma.

Observations of some variable X-ray sources within the Milky Way's center that have shown no outbursts in over a decade have led some researchers to suggest a significant population of stellar mass black holes in the region. A crucial aspect of the theory that these sources are actually black holes is the claim that neutron star binaries with low masses exhibit recurring X-ray bursts within short intervals. This study contradicts that idea by revealing that about half of the known LMXBs, featuring a neutron star as the primary component, exhibit outburst recurrence times exceeding a decade when detected by the MAXI telescope. Moreover, to reconcile the total population of neutron star binaries with observed and radio pulsar populations within the Milky Way, researchers find that a significant majority of these binaries have recurrence times exceeding a century for outbursts visible to the MAXI telescope and most remain undiscovered.

THz radiation enables the precise stimulation of vibrational frequencies in molecules and crystals, leading to the introduction of inertial influences on electrons. By drawing a comparison to classical mechanics, where circular motion generates Coriolis and centrifugal forces, analogous effects arise, specifically spin-rotation coupling, centrifugal field coupling, and the interplay of these forces with the spin-orbit and the redshift of energy levels. These effects can persist for a few picoseconds following the initial stimulation, and potentially amplifying their magnitude could make this approach a promising means of controlling localized quantum states and chemical reaction barriers via vibration.

Improving neural conversational agents' ability to produce diverse, engaging responses in casual conversations is a challenge. To tackle this issue, our research introduces two significant innovations. Firstly, we investigate the application of Natural Language Inference (NLI) models in enhancing response diversity by semantic measures, as the diversity expected in conversations mirrors that anticipated in NLI tasks. Our experiments indicate that incorporating an MNL-based method results in a 10% increase in semantic diversity with no decline in response quality. Building on this, our study's second contribution develops a hybrid model that integrates the MNL approach with a diverse ensemble of neural assemblies, demonstrating a 15% improvement in response diversity while maintaining performance. All code and data are available at https://github.com/cristian98/nli-dia.

The occurrence of sustainable hydrogen burning in very low-mass stars might be impacted by rotation due to the addition of centrifugal force and potential break-up caused by rapid spinning. Computer simulations model rotating low-mass stars with the capability for sustained nuclear reactions, considering a range of rotation rates, rather than slow rotation alone. Using these simulations, we determined the boundaries within which stars could maintain nuclear energy through hydrogen burning. These boundaries varied based on angular momentum. However, above a certain threshold (approximately 8.85 x 10^48 erg s) the boundaries broke into two distinct branches, resulting from objects losing mass and experiencing extreme spin. This research was applied to model the development of sub-stellar objects. Two possible scenarios were modeled: one with external forces gradually slowing the star, mainly controlled by spin-down time, and another where the star spins out of control, ultimately shedding mass and shrinking.

The technique of amplitude analysis in hadron decay studies is quite effective, 
However, this analysis faces a major challenge in addressing instrumental influences 
such as fluctuations in background levels and selection efficiency across different 
multidimensional kinematic scenarios.  This article will review traditional methods 
used for calculating efficiency and background probability and discuss the application 
of two techniques specifically density estimation using Gaussian processes and 
artificial neural networks. Although widely adopted in other contexts, these methods 
have not been heavily employed for amplitude analyses. The article also introduces 
new applications for these models, such as leveraging sidebands to determine the 
density of background in multiple dimensions, as well as more comprehensive density 
estimation utilizing artificial neural networks.

A new model based on a comprehensive expression for radiation energy has been proposed, and it effectively explains the past and predicts the future of extreme gamma-ray burst dynamics during the power-law phase.  By examining two phases of extreme gamma-ray burst dynamics during both the radiation-dominated and hydrodynamical sweep-up stages, the model provides detailed explanations for observed burst dynamics and light curve breaks.  By analyzing high-energy extreme gamma-ray bursts, the model yields precise estimates for key burst characteristics such as particle per burst, total energy per burst, and duration of the burst.  When applied to the unusual burst GBN 19/10/19 within a new regime of extreme gamma-ray bursts, the model offers a plausible explanation for its atypical dynamics.

Bipartite graphs depicting connections between distinct groups of objects have numerous practical applications, and their visualization often takes the form of a 2-tier layout where corresponding entities are aligned horizontally across two parallel lines, connected by lines representing relationships between them. The task of reducing edge crossings within these visualizations can be computationally intensive, yet might not always guarantee sufficiently low crossings levels to maintain the visualization's clarity. In contrast, an approach has been developed to remove edge crossings by splitting specific nodes, targeting the minimum number required to yield an edge-free (planar) drawing. The question of determining if an edge-free drawing is possible by breaking at most a specified number of nodes within the context of general graphs is solvable in a time frame that is exponential only in relation to this number. However, for bipartite graphs, an improved solution is possible with a reduced exponential factor.

This paper will present our approach to optimizing bipedal robot walking assisted by thrusters using a closed-loop feedback system. By assuming that supervisory controllers are properly optimized, we will concentrate on executing gaits with assistance from thrusters. To achieve this, we will: present a model-based supervisory controller that ensures the successful completion of thruster-assisted gaits; and: utilize a throughtful evaluation method across various scenarios of blocked joints and lost thrusters to assess the robustness of our feedback controller in comparison to a feedback-less approach.

Becker-Denef-Lipschitz first observed in 1979 that over finite fields $k$, the total residue map $\text{res}$ from Laurent series to $k$ is expressible in a specific language, provided $t$ is included as a parameter. This discovery motivated further research into the properties of a specific mathematical theory related to valued fields. In the course of these investigations, the authors proved that this theory does not have a certain desirable feature and demonstrated that, for infinite fields $k$, the associated power series fields cannot be computationally decided. This, in turn, led to an analogous undecidability conclusion for a specific complex-valued field of power series.

In order to enhance side-channel attacks, this research introduces a new side-channel primitive called a Hyper-Threading Attack (HTA), which is based on an unanticipated side effect of the CPU's hyper-threading design.  To make this attack feasible, two existing side effects resulting from HTA are made measurable for the first time, which are the impact on cache access latency and memory access timing.  To accomplish this, a novel method is used to deliberately slow down and systematically test CPU frequency responses to external interruptions.  Furthermore, a new procedure is developed to automatically generate side-effect-inducing shell scripts.  With the HTA-based side effect, a more subtle and harder-to-detect root access password extraction is demonstrated, which is in contrast to existing implementations that rely on other methods.  To further support side-channel analysis, an open-source library is also released to facilitate future research.

A localized alteration in knot diagrams is referred to as an unknotting operation. It can be demonstrated that any knot diagram can be converted into a trivial unknot through a sequence of unknotting operations, combined with some variations in the diagram configuration, which are referred to as Reidemeister moves. Unknotting operations hold significant value in the field of knot theory, contributing to variables such as the crossing reduction index and being utilized in diverse applications. The current study comprises three main aspects: Firstly, a novel unnamed unknotting operation is introduced for classical links, which preserves the Kauffman bracket polynomial and results in words at the fundamental quandle and the conjugacy quandle. Secondly, the same unknotting operation is adapted for the purpose of welded links. Thirdly, algorithms are developed to ascertain if the welded versions of two links are equivalent, which rely on properties such as the Conjugacy quandle and a new unnamed property, along with the impact of the novel unknotting operation being examined.

We've demonstrated that combining the 1-cocycle of a long knot's space with Fox-Hatcher 1-cycles through integration produces a specific Vassiliev invariant, having a precise order of three. This discovery builds on a preceding finding by the second listed author, proving that I(H1(Y)) produces a Vassiliev invariant of order two related to the Coxeter invariant. Nevertheless, unlike the Coxeter invariant, the I(H1(Y)) integration produces multiple invariants of order three, which differ by the dimension of certain homology groups of a three-manifold, resulting from handling the incompressible tori in the invariant's expression. Furthermore, we establish that the I(H1(Y)) integration produces only a finite set of independent invariants of order three, directly relating to the dimension of a specific homology group.

In cooperative systems with multiple agents, coordination enables tasks to be performed that would be beyond the capabilities of any single agent. We investigate the concept of coordination through strategic decision-making, focusing on a scenario where agents select between two tasks of varying difficulty that are randomly distributed and partially known. It has been established that when the distribution of tasks is uniform, a strategy exists where the agents split into two groups, each working on the same more difficult task. When the distribution is uniform but varies in difficulty, our analysis shows that for uniform prior beliefs, the agents adopt the same strategy from the previous case. However, when the distribution of tasks is non-uniform, we found that the most beneficial outcome is achieved when the agents divide into groups proportional to the task difficulty. When communication among the agents is limited, it has been observed that a situation with stable and predictable cycle lengths results in the most advantageous outcome, where the agents split into groups of equal size during each cycle.
